eligibility_note: Own panel estimation, 97 economies 2010-2020, composite ICT/internet/broadband/mobile-based index, income inequality outcome (family 4) plus income-group comparison.

results.quote: DEDI significantly negatively affects income disparity
Model (3) demonstrates the result of the two-stage instrumental variable method (IV-2SLS)
globalization weakens the influence of DEDI on promoting equality
for LMICs, DEDI is prone to improve income disparity
DEDI significantly reduces the income share of the top 10 %
DEDI has no significant effects on the share of the bottom 10 % of the population globally

income_group_note: Values match Table 6-8. Low-income merged into lower-middle as stated; Table A3 lower-middle column includes low-income economies (e.g. Liberia, Mozambique, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Uganda, Togo, South Sudan).

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: causal language, IV (1984 telephone lines x CSG) with weak exclusion argument, no country FE in IV, 50x FE estimate
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: entropy composite mixes ICT with R&D, patents, human capital
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: 97 of 147 with no stated rule; but record is wrong that no low-income country is listed
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: headline rests on p<0.1 in FE with year effects
risk_of_bias.why: Causal claims with FE and a questionable IV; serious fits.
